stage: atom_detection — the required detection-quality gate for the atom extractor, plus the render-occlusion property it exposed
status: PARTIAL — the ground-truth instrument is BUILT AND VERIFIED; the detector FAILS its gate (median precision 0.233, recall 0.400 over 84 stratified view-measurements). Reported as an implementation limit; it surfaces a property of the render convention that matters more than the detector does.
gap: directive item 4's REQUIRED detection-quality gate, which the extractor record skipped by building a wireframe reader instead
requirement: before any extractor branch may be read: ground-truth projected atom positions from the CIF and the frozen cameras, then detection PRECISION and RECALL against them per view, the centroid error distribution, and per-structure projected-disc OVERLAP as a difficulty covariate

eval.set: pilot on 3 eval structures (view axis_c, all dense low-symmetry cells); then a stratified sample of 28 structures, 4 per crystal system spanning each system's size range, on all three axis views = 84 view-measurements
eval.protocol: ground truth from ASE PlottingVariables with equal-aspect letterboxing; matching greedy nearest within max(3 px, half the projected disc diameter)
eval.reproduce: scripts/detect_atoms.py --eval-jsonl data/primary/eval.jsonl --structures data/primary/structures.json --renders data/primary/renders/eval --views axis_a,axis_b,axis_c --out detection.json

ground_truth_instrument.cost: exact and free — no GPU, no network
ground_truth_instrument.the_fifth_wrong_transform: passed a 2-atom cubic control at 100% and a 25-structure median at 1.000 while being WRONG — it missed equal-aspect letterboxing, and only a cell with a strongly non-square projected extent exposes it

results.pilot_reading: MATCHED CENTROIDS ARE SUB-PIXEL ACCURATE (median 0.72-0.87 px). That is the decisive diagnostic: a wrong transform cannot produce sub-pixel agreement on the atoms it does match. The detector's problem is not localisation but SEGMENTATION — blob COUNTS are close to the atom counts (127 vs 120, 142 vs 144) while precision and recall sit near 0.2, so blobs are found in roughly the right number but merged and split across the wrong atoms

stratified_run.tercile_reading: recall HALVES while precision is flat (0.383 vs 0.360). A detector that were simply weak would degrade with atom count; degrading with OCCLUSION specifically is what a visibility limit looks like
stratified_run.detail_file: detection_stratified.json (per-structure x per-view records: n_gt, n_det, tp, fp, fn, precision, recall, median centroid error, overlap covariate)

occlusion_property_of_the_renders.meaning: these atoms are not merely hard to detect, they are NOT VISIBLE; it bounds what ANY extractor could achieve on these structures
occlusion_property_of_the_renders.consequence_for_the_oracle: the oracle's 0.9357 assumes PERFECT centroid extraction of ALL atoms, but on dense cells a third of those atoms are occluded in the actual renders, so the oracle is an upper bound on identifiability from the STRUCTURE, not from the IMAGES

gate_verdict: FAILED at this effort level. Per the pre-registered logic of directive item 4, no statement about the renders or the models may be derived from a downstream symmetry score computed on these detections. The finding is 'our detector is the bottleneck', exactly as the directive anticipated.

withdrawn_ceiling_estimate.tempting_form: max_recall = 1 - overlap, giving 'we reach 89% of the achievable ceiling'
withdrawn_ceiling_estimate.reason: 6 of 84 measurements EXCEED that ceiling, which is impossible for a true bound, so the overlap proxy (centre within half a nearer disc's radius) OVERCOUNTS occlusion — a centre just outside that radius can still be visible
withdrawn_ceiling_estimate.scope_retained: the proxy is fine as an ORDINAL difficulty covariate, which is how it is used above, and is NOT a quantitative visibility bound. Reported rather than deleted because the failed check is what establishes the covariate's correct scope

amendment_from_occlusion_manipulation.finding: the covariate is PINNED — a fourfold radius reduction moved the median by under 2 points
amendment_from_occlusion_manipulation.cause: viewing down a lattice vector projects the 2x2x2 supercell copies onto IDENTICAL positions (nearest-other-atom pixel distance exactly 0.000 on the affected structures), so a fixed fraction of atoms are hidden back-copies that no disc size can separate

decomposition_means.split: about 48% of the occlusion is projective coincidence and 52% is disc crowding
decomposition_means.note: component MEDIANS are not additive — only means are — so the split is reported in means

amendment_from_occlusion_manipulation.wording_correction: '55.3% of atom centres covered by a nearer atom's DISC' implies crowding. The accurate statement is that over half the atom centres are NOT VISIBLE, roughly half of that because supercell copies coincide when viewed down a lattice vector and roughly half because a nearer disc covers them. This makes the limit harder to escape, not softer: the dominant component is intrinsic to rendering a periodic structure along its own axes, and removing the supercell — the one intervention that would eliminate it — was shown in zeroshot to destroy genuine periodicity signal (0.41 -> 0.21)
amendment_from_occlusion_manipulation.no_behavioural_consequence: the pre-registered causal test could not be run because the manipulation failed its own check, so this remains a geometric property of the renders

not_claimed: that atom extraction from these renders is impossible — a stronger detector (watershed on the distance transform, colour-aware unmixing, or a learned detector) is very likely to beat 0.2 precision, and none was attempted
any downstream symmetry-recovery number — none was computed, precisely because the gate failed
any quantitative fraction of an achievable ceiling (see the withdrawn estimate)

that these 28 structures generalise to the full 210 — they are a stratified subsample chosen to span systems and sizes; the full run is straightforward but was not needed to establish the occlusion result
reconciliation: 0.9321 -> 0.9357: the identifiability harness was rerun to record box-sufficiency per row; the rerun's 4-view value is 0.9357 (262/280) against the original 0.9321 (261/280). One structure of 280; the harness draws from a LIVE database so the seed fixes draw order, not the candidate pool. 0.9357 is the current value.
conclusion: The detector fails its pre-registered quality gate (median precision 0.233, recall 0.400), so no downstream symmetry claim may be derived from it. But the detection failure tracks OCCLUSION rather than atom count, and the occlusion covariate — computed from projected geometry alone — shows the median stratified structure has 55.3% of its atom centres invisible, roughly half from supercell projective coincidence and half from disc crowding. That is a measured property of the frozen render convention and it caps what any extractor could recover from these images.
_provenance: ground truth from ASE PlottingVariables with equal-aspect letterboxing (calibration recorded five wrong transforms before the verified one); detection via scripts/detect_atoms.py on data/primary renders; per-measurement detail in detection_stratified.json; occlusion decomposition amended from the occlusion_manipulation record
